results.reply: "Welcome to Darcy's Pub, young fella. I'm Padraig, the publican, and I'll be glad to pour ye a pint and get ye settled."
"Ah, Mrs. O'Connor, 'tis a fine morning for a visit, isn't it? Come in out of the rain and warm yourself by the fire, I've a fresh pot of tea brewin'."
"Ah, now, Mrs. O'Connor, it's a pleasure to see ye, even on a chill day like this. What brings ye out on a Sunday, when most folks are in the pews?"
"Welcome, love, I'm Brigid, the midwife. What brings ye to our neck o' the woods?"
"Ah, Moira, 'tis a grand morning for a visit, don't you think? Come in out of the damp and warm yourself by the fire."
"Ah, Kathleen, isn't it a grand day to be out and about, even if it's as misty as a blessing from the saints?"
"Ah, good evenin' to ye, stranger. I am Father Donnellan, the parish priest of this fair village, here at Darcy's Pub."
"Ah, Seamus, 'tis a dreary morn, isn't it? Come in, and let us sit by the fire for a moment, I've just brewed a pot of tea."
"Ah, Seamus, what brings you out on a day so damp and dreary? Come in, come in, and let us speak of the scriptures, for the Lord's word will bring warmth to a soul chilled by the morning mist."
"Ah, good evenin' to ye, I'm Sean Murphy, farmer from the bog, what brings ye to our humble pub?"
